title: RAW UNREVIEWED: independently visible figure action binds bath-text roles
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. On an already admitted bath page, a physically unambiguous depicted action, if one is independently established, could bind a participant as agent, patient, or recipient across a whole owned prose block. Rival complete readings assign the same recurring words to an impersonal station or bath operation. The candidate must read every group in the nominated block with one fixed role rule and carry that rule into other admitted blocks with the same graphic action; the rival must do the same. GDT590's body/station split and GDT595's object completions are hypothetical contextual readings, not independent gesture-to-word bindings. GDT790's panel ownership does not assign individual words to figures; the old inline figure cardinality route failed singular ownership. No particular gesture, actor or word is currently certified, so there is no experiment-ready target or claim of progress. No new page, reserve, or sealed data is proposed.

design.mechanism: A separately established physical figure action fixes the agent-patient-recipient relation that a complete owned bath passage must express.
design.unit: One whole already admitted graphic owner plus its complete prose block, then all admitted blocks with the same independently defined action.
design.contrast: Participant-action reading with one persistent actor and affected object versus impersonal station/bath-operation reading with no actor carry.
design.prediction: A fixed participant reading must place the independently identified actor, object, and transfer direction consistently in every full matching block, including later references; an impersonal rival predicts station or vessel continuity instead and must explain the same complete words. A nonmatching visible action or a block requiring opposite role direction defeats the respective model. Present blocker: neither singular action ownership nor an independent lexical bridge is established.
design.scope: exploratory semantic proposal; no fixed test selected
